A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRE Suite and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–E. Retained material, relocations, and additions can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V3 reports original geo-localization evaluations, GREval-Bench results, training-stage ablations, and additional Google StreetView evaluations in Tables 2–4 and 6–7.

after.justification: V4 retains the original empirical results and adds OSV-5M evaluations and ablations using additional model configurations in Tables 8–9.

M1.justification: The cold-start SFT, two-stage GRPO training, reward functions, and inference prompts are retained. Appendix C.1 newly describes progressive reward-threshold refinement, but v3 did not specify a fixed schedule; this adds training documentation without establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Table 8 adds evaluation on OSV-5M, which v3 only cited. This extends the evaluated image data within the existing worldwide street-image geolocation task. The previously used training datasets and evaluation benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds GeoReasoner, its coordinate-prompted variant, and SeekWorld on both benchmarks, plus Qwen2.5-VL-7B, LLaVA-v1.5-7B, and Molmo-D-7B on Im2GPS3k. Table 8 additionally includes SC Retrieval and RFM S2. These substantially broaden the comparisons beyond v3's traditional geolocators in Table 2.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce average distance on OSV-5M and training-stage comparisons using Qwen2.5-VL-32B and LLaVA-v1.5-7B. Table 2 distinguishes coordinate-prompted GeoReasoner from its default city-output setting. Existing sample allocations and accuracy thresholds are retained; detailed OSV-5M split and sample information is not supplied.

E4.justification: Table 9 extends v3's Qwen2.5-VL-7B stage ablations to Qwen2.5-VL-32B on both main benchmarks and tests SFT/Stage II contributions for LLaVA on Im2GPS3k. This substantially expands analysis of model-scale and model-family generality. Appendix D.1 also adds an inference-computation comparison; existing qualitative cases remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point results without repeated-run counts, random-seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added tables and revised descriptive percentages introduce no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Existing results in Tables 2–4 and 6–7 are retained, but substantial new entries appear. Table 2 adds default GeoReasoner's 65.4% accuracy at 750 km on GWS15k, where GRE remains 54.8%. Tables 8–9 add benchmark and ablation results, and Appendix D.1 adds FLOP measurements. Figure 4 revises explicit/implicit indicator shares from 25.8%/72.1% to 26.4%/73.6%.

T1.justification: The GRPO objectives, geodesic-distance and reward definitions in Equations 1–5, and CoT-quality formula in Equation 6 are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, theoretical results, proofs, or derivations appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list, and conclusion retain the same dataset/model/benchmark contributions and open-ended geolocation claims. The abstract's broad claim of superiority across all granularities also remains unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 removes the claimed GWS15k 750-km superiority and adds an explanation involving learned world knowledge. Section 3.1 newly asserts that geographic filtering addresses landmark-repetition risks, without documenting a corresponding new filtering procedure. The appendix adds interpretations about broader model applicability and contextualizes inference costs as a limitation.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 newly describes reward-threshold refinement, although numerical thresholds and update criteria remain unspecified. Section 5 changes the reported hardware from 16 to 8 NVIDIA H20 GPUs, resolving disagreement with v3's existing Appendix D.1 statement. V4 also identifies THOP for FLOP measurement and adds pointers to repository materials.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds brief discussion and citations concerning diffusion/flow matching, RL-trained decision agents, and Kimi-VL. Comparison-related references are added, RLAIF-V is removed, and the cited OpenAI documentation changes from o3-mini to o3/o4-mini. GRE's central positioning as a reasoning-based geolocator remains stable.

P1.justification: V4 adds Xiaojun Ye to the author list, changes 'extra information' terminology to 'prior knowledge,' inserts short explanatory passages, and adds Appendix C.3 while renumbering the qualitative-results subsection. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 expands and gains a caption explaining the GeoReasoner variants; Tables 8–9 are new. Figure 2 labels change, and existing material, including Table 4 and Figure 13, moves as text reflows. The overall visual style and existing qualitative illustrations are retained.

improvement.justification: V4 strengthens scrutiny of GRE's comparative advantage through relevant reasoning-based competitors and tests training-stage benefits beyond the original 7B backbone. It also quantifies inference costs and resolves the GPU-count inconsistency. These improve empirical support and transparency, although new evaluation settings remain incompletely documented and the abstract's universal superiority claim remains unqualified despite contrary entries in Tables 2 and 8.
